description.narrative: CERIM KRI is a behaviour change programme designed to reduce irregular migration from the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI) to the UK and France through evidence-based community engagement, strategic communications, and digital innovation. Drawing on target audience analysis and continuous monitoring and evaluation, the programme addresses the social and behavioural factors that influence migration decisions and adapts its interventions based on emerging evidence. Working with young people, families, educators, religious leaders, civil society organisations, and government stakeholders, CERIM KRI delivers tailored awareness-raising activities, capacity-building workshops, community storytelling, and targeted digital outreach that challenge misinformation, promote informed decision-making, and increase awareness of the risks of irregular migration alongside safe, legal, local and sustainable alternatives. By strengthening the capacity of trusted local actors and fostering community ownership, the programme encourages more resilient communities and supports young people to make informed decisions based on realistic expectations and local opportunities.
